Namespace ParquetNeo

Classes

BloomFilterSettings

A bloom filter for a column, see ColumnBloomFilters.

ColumnReader

Reads the values of one column chunk, a batch at a time. Obtain it from OpenColumn(int) and dispose it when done, which returns its buffers to the pool.

ColumnWriter

Writes the values of one column of a row group. Obtain it from NextColumn(), call one of the Write… methods one or more times, then move on to the next column.

DictionarySettings

How one column is dictionary encoded; see ColumnDictionaries.

FilterColumn

A column a condition is put on; see Column(params string[]).

ParquetFileReader

Reads a Parquet file one row group and one leaf column at a time, with the definition and repetition levels of nested columns. The stream must be readable and seekable, because the metadata sits at the end of the file.

ParquetFileWriter

Writes a Parquet file, one row group at a time. Columns are written one leaf column at a time, with the definition and repetition levels for nested ones. The stream only needs to be writable: offsets are counted rather than read from the stream, so it need not be seekable.

ParquetFilter

A condition on the values of columns, which a reader checks against the statistics of each row group (the smallest and largest value, and how many are null) to skip the row groups that cannot hold a row that satisfies it. Build one with Column(params string[]) and combine with And(ParquetFilter), Or(ParquetFilter) and Not().

ParquetReaderOptions

Settings for a ParquetFileReader. The limits protect against corrupt or hostile files.

ParquetWriterOptions

Settings for a ParquetFileWriter.

RowGroupReader

Gives access to the columns of one row group.

RowGroupWriter

Writes one row group: every column of the schema, in schema order, each with the same number of rows. Create it with AppendRowGroup(), call NextColumn() once per column, and dispose it (or call Close()) to finish the group.

RowSelection

Some rows of a row group, as ascending runs that do not touch. Given to OpenColumn(int, RowSelection) so that the column is read for only those rows; the pages that hold none of them are not read. Rows count from the first of the group, and a row of a repeated column is a whole record (a list), however many values it has.
